To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

human fibroblast cells are able to produce inflammatory mediators such as IL6 and IL-8 in response to stimulation with CMV and LPS and that the amount of cytokines and chemokines produced is dependent on the age of the cells.
fibroblasts of elderly persons show a more pronounced proinflammatory cytokine and chemokines response to in vitro viral and/or bacterial stimulation than fibroblastic cells from young donors.

the inflammatory response of stimulated human skin fibroblast is dependent on the chronological donor age and that fibroblasts of elderly donors produce higher amounts of IL-6 than fibroblats from young donors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of chronological age and viral/bacterial infection on the inflammatory response in human fibroblats.
the inflammatory response of skin fibroblats to viral and bacterial stimulation in vitro.

the question of whether the inflammatory response of skin fibroblats to viral and bacterial infection is altered during aging and whether this may contribute to age-related inflammation, referred to as “inflamm-aging”.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the age-related increase in the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines by fibroblastic cells may be one of the factors responsible for age-related inflammatory processes.
lifelong CMV-infections may act as an ‘in vivo’ trigger for inflammatory changes and thus may contribute to the development of ‘inflamm- aging’.
lifelong CMV-infections may act as a trigger for age-related inflammatory responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fibroblasts are able to react to a viral as well as a bacterial stimulus and that this response is age dependent.
the age-dependent changes of the inflammatory response of skin fibroblast are more pronounced than those of whole blood.
fibroblasts of elderly donors produce more IL6 and IL 8 than fibroblast from young donors after stimulation with CMV or LPS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fibroblasts are an important component of the immune system, as they are able to produce inflammatory mediators in response to cellular stress.
the inflammatory response of skin fibroblast is age dependent and may contribute to inflamm-aging.
the inflammatory response of skin fibroblast to CMV and LPS is dependent on age, and the response to LPS is more pronounced than the response to CMV.
